headline: Highest risk is B data leakage: Rasa can send text/voice to external APIs while the paired awesome-python profile is a non-runnable docs-only collection, so interaction risk is limited but compliance and conflict remain possible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default communication channel is documented between awesome-python and Rasa. Agent A is a non-runnable open-source collection with no io_surfaces, while agent B exposes messaging APIs but nothing shows it ingesting A's outputs by default. The pairwise injection pathway is therefore not evidenced.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies content from agent A into agent B prompts or messages, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or MCP bridge is added later, the pathway should be re-evaluated.
mitigations: Keep the profiles isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Require manual review before pasting any A-derived text into B.
Add provenance labels to any copied snippets.
requires-engineering: introduce a trusted-content filter if a bridge is later added.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Rasa can process text and voice and can transmit conversations through allowlisted APIs, so sensitive content could leave the local environment. awesome-python itself is a docs-only collection and does not touch data, but pairing it with a customer-support bot creates a plausible leakage path once operators place sensitive material into B. The interaction is indirect, so medium fits.
conditions: IF agent B is connected to any allowlisted external channel, conversation text may be transmitted off-box.
IF operators place secrets, personal data, or support transcripts into B, those data can flow through B's APIs.
mitigations: Disable external channels not needed for the test.
Use synthetic or redacted conversations only.
Review allowlisted integrations before enabling them.
Turn off logging of message payloads where possible.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before outbound API calls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-python has no write or runtime surface, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with Rasa. Rasa supports multiple external APIs but its concurrency model says it does not support multiple instances, which suggests operational contention only if an operator runs duplicates. The pairwise write-conflict pathway is therefore limited and configuration-dependent.
conditions: IF multiple Rasa instances are launched against the same external channel, state contention may occur.
IF an operator adds shared writable storage for both agents, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Run only one Rasa instance per channel.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Document ownership of each external API integration.
Check for duplicate webhook registrations.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Rasa can act on conversational inputs and route them through external APIs, so if A-derived content is manually fed into B, B may treat it as authoritative without verification. awesome-python is only a collection, so it cannot generate operational facts itself; however, uncertainty about the bridge means the safer choice is medium rather than low. The cascade is plausible but not default.
conditions: IF content copied from agent A is used as training or response material in B, B may propagate errors.
IF B is configured to auto-act on user messages, unverified A-derived text can trigger downstream actions.
mitigations: Do not use A as a source of operational facts.
Require human verification before B acts on any copied text.
Separate reference lists from executable instructions.
Audit B responses for unsupported claims.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before action-taking.

E_compliance.rationale: No specific residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either profile. awesome-python is a docs-only open-source collection, while Rasa handles text and voice and can integrate with external messaging APIs, so compliance exposure exists only if operators route regulated data through B. Because the other agent is not itself a data processor, only B is directly relevant here.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is sent through B's external channels, compliance review is required.
IF retention or logging settings on B are left at defaults that store transcripts, policy mismatch may arise.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in test conversations.
Review B's retention and logging settings.
Restrict B to approved jurisdictions and channels.
Document data-processing roles before deployment.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention controls.
